significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that, for an unchanged target, increasing “benign context-complexity, not raw prompt length” predictably raises both a pre-generation difficulty signal and reasoning-token use, while “resetting that difficulty representation cancels the tax at equal accuracy.” This combines a form-(iii) relation between context complexity, decoded difficulty, and compute with a form-(ii) mechanism: the phenomenon fixes expected compute under new irrelevant-context conditions, while the causal reset identifies why it changes; this bears directly on difficulty-dependent allocation assumptions used in adaptive test-time-compute work such as Snell et al. (2024). The claim is determinate, and a negative result would distinguish no contamination, a pure-length effect, or a generic attention mechanism, although it would not invalidate adaptive compute generally. In the topic-substitution check, generic efficient reasoning would not earn this score: the added value comes specifically from the complexity-to-difficulty-to-compute coupling and its causal separation from raw length and target difficulty.

reach.justification: The named handles are the “pre-generation difficulty representation,” “prompt sanitation,” and an “inference-time difficulty-reset controller,” giving both a diagnostic quantity and an intervention. They are ex ante because the readout and reset occur at the prompt boundary before reasoning tokens are generated, leaving RAG or chat systems an action window to strip context, reset the signal, or alter compute allocation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction still travels as a relation—greater benign context complexity should raise decoded difficulty and token use—although the asserted scope is limited to reasoning-model families, several reasoning tasks, and realistic irrelevant RAG passages rather than arbitrary architectures or modalities. Downstream users include practitioners who audit or ship RAG and chat systems, not only mechanism researchers; the topic-substitution check would leave no comparable handle, so the score derives from these specific predictors and controls rather than from efficient reasoning as a broad topic.
